title: Demonstrate Reliability and Business Continuity Through Operations
objective: Operate availability, backups, recovery, and validation according to the scope of failures and recovery objectives.

prerequisites.title: Operate observation through remediation as one continuous process

sections.title: Set recovery objectives for each type of failure
paragraphs: The service owner does not treat a single-instance failure, an Availability Zone failure, accidental deletion, and a Region failure as the same event. They establish recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs) based on business requirements, then select the required redundancy, backups, and recovery procedures for each failure scope.

High availability is not simply a matter of increasing the number of resources. Verify that the system behaves as expected during a failure by checking health checks, failover triggers, data consistency, and the user journey after recovery.

sections.title: Backups are complete only when restoration is tested
paragraphs: Backup personnel do not treat a backup success notification alone as evidence that recovery is possible. They determine the backup frequency, retention period, encryption, permissions to restore, restoration destination, and the data integrity checks to perform after restoration.

In restoration drills, they carry out the restoration process by assigning who restores what and in which order, and by verifying what must be checked before the application can connect. They compare the drill results with the RTO and RPO, and improve the procedures or configuration for any unmet requirements.

sections.title: Distinguishing Load Fluctuations from Failures
paragraphs: Operations staff do not mistake increased load for a failure. They check metrics that indicate demand and metrics that indicate resource saturation, and verify the Auto Scaling minimum, maximum, and desired capacity, health checks, and the settings required for startup.

Caches, queues, and deployment across multiple AZs help limit the propagation of load or failures. However, operational inconsistencies cannot be prevented unless cache freshness, queue retries and duplicates, and the write destination after failover are defined.

checkpoints.prompt: The operations manager for a payment service is creating a plan for a single-AZ failure and accidental deletion. Select the one most appropriate task to perform first.

choices.text: Handle all failures using the same procedure and do not record recovery objectives.
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to assess the required availability or data protection.

choices.text: Define RTO and RPO for each type of failure based on business requirements, and map redundancy and recovery procedures to them.
choices.explanation: The required protection method varies depending on the scope of the failure and the recovery objectives.

choices.text: Do not create recovery procedures in advance, so that personnel can decide what to do during a failure.
choices.explanation: The response time and outcome will depend on the personnel involved.

checkpoints.prompt: A database backup administrator must select the single most appropriate method for verifying recoverability.

choices.text: Check only the success status displayed for the backup job.
choices.explanation: This does not verify the restoration time or availability after restoration.

choices.text: Perform a restore in an isolated restoration target, then verify post-restoration integrity, permissions, and application connectivity.
choices.explanation: This verifies the actual recovery procedure rather than merely confirming that a backup exists.

choices.text: Keep only the latest backup without checking the retention period.
choices.explanation: This may fail to meet RPO or audit-related retention requirements.

checkpoints.prompt: As the number of orders increases, response times are deteriorating. Select the single most appropriate item an operations team should verify when reviewing the Auto Scaling configuration.

choices.text: Increase only the maximum capacity without limit and disable health checks.
choices.explanation: This could leave failed instances in service and increase costs and the scope of the failure.

choices.text: Always add instances manually without checking the impact on users.
choices.explanation: This does not ensure reproducibility or a sufficiently rapid response.

choices.text: Verify the metrics that indicate demand and saturation, the minimum, maximum, and desired capacity, health checks, and launch-time settings.
choices.explanation: This confirms, together with the operational conditions, whether the system can keep up with fluctuations in load.
